judge_panel.reason: The paper explicitly states the 11-second time limit is for the MILP oracle used 'exclusively offline' as a supervisor, not for real-time deployment: 'MILP runtimes correspond to the end-to-end solver time per instance using Google OR-Tools, executed in multi-thread mode with a per-instance time limit of 11 s' and 'Due to its combinatorial complexity, the MILP is not intended for real-time deployment.' The sub-30 ms requirement applies to GP-MILP and GINE inference, not the oracle, so there is no contradiction.

The paper explicitly distinguishes the offline MILP oracle from the real-time method: "Due to its combinatorial complexity, the MILP is not intended for real-time deployment" and "The MILP formulation is run entirely offline during the dataset generation stage and has no effect on runtime performance." The sub-30 ms claim is made for the hybrid method, not the oracle: "GP-MILP execution times stay below 30 ms for nearly all graph instances."

The reviewer's concern is unfounded because the paper explicitly states that the MILP is an offline component, noting, 'Due to its combinatorial complexity, the MILP is not intended for real-time deployment' and is used 'exclusively offline to generate ground-truth relay configurations'.
